verdict.rationale: Jules is designed for end-to-end autonomous implementation: it clones the repo, plans, edits code, and opens a PR (jules-docs-3, jules-docs-4, jules-docs-7, jules-docs-8), and community reports confirm it produces usable PRs and is particularly good at writing tests for isolated functions (jules-comm-6, jules-comm-11). However, hands-on evidence shows inconsistent reliability — it can get stuck in loops, fail on complex/monorepo codebases, need babysitting, and produce lower-quality code than competitors (jules-comm-9, jules-comm-13, jules-comm-15, jules-comm-18), and success is reported at ~75% rather than guaranteed. missing for 10: consistent reliability on complex end-to-end feature tasks, stronger independent quality benchmarks, and confirmation that generated tests are comprehensive rather than only for isolated functions.
